claim: Let \(k=\mathbb F_q\) and \(L=ke\oplus kf\) with \([e,f]=f\). Every 2-local automorphism \(\Phi:L\to L\) is uniquely determined by a permutation \(\sigma\) of \(k\) and a scalar \(\kappa\in k^\times\), via \(\Phi(ae+bf)=ae+a\sigma(b/a)f\) for \(a\ne0\) and \(\Phi(bf)=\kappa bf\) on the line \(a=0\). Consequently there are exactly \(q!(q-1)\) such maps, of which \(q(q-1)\) are automorphisms, and every 2-local automorphism is an automorphism if and only if \(q=2\).

correctness.rationale: The automorphism group is derived from the characteristic derived ideal \( [L,L]=kf \) and the defining bracket. 2-locality on scalar multiples gives homogeneity; pairs on two distinct nonvertical lines force the slope parameter to be injective, hence bijective over the finite field. The converse is verified by explicit witnesses for every pair type. The exact count follows from the unique parameters (permutation, nonzero vertical scale).

value.rationale: This is a complete classification, not merely an example or a finite experiment: it identifies every possibly nonlinear 2-local automorphism and counts them exactly for every finite field. The sharp boundary at \(q=2\) separates the smallest field, where all such maps are genuine automorphisms, from every larger finite field, where exotic maps exist. This provides a natural baseline for finite-field studies of local symmetry in solvable Lie algebras.
